digest.component_or_area: CI/CD workflows - pytest execution across external and live-service lanes
propositions: Eight CI workflow lanes lacked per-test hang guards, allowing deadlocked tests to hide without traceback or identification behind final output dots
Per-test timeout budgets were calibrated from historical runtime data using the rule: at least 10x the lane's observed mean per-test duration, floored at 300 seconds

Detection rule requires every pytest-invoking step in .github/workflows files to carry both --timeout and --timeout-method=thread flags, enforced by exhaustive workflow parsing that discards shell comments and matches pytest commands at boundaries

External live-service lanes (external-llm, external-jira, langfuse-trace, jira-dc-harness) and offline unit test lanes received per-test budgets ranging from 300s to 3600s based on observed step durations and operational requirements

The parity assertion in test_ci_workflow_parity.py was replaced with an exhaustive sweep over all workflows using the new detection rule, covering four pytest invocation forms and validated against known near-misses to prevent false positives

All 11 acceptance criteria were verified on the merged change including timeout values per lane, pytest-timeout dependency installed in minimal environments, and CI green across all 22 jobs and 7 mutation shards
